summary: Lookout at Granite Park Chalet in 1930, per an NPS report quoted by Montana Lookouts; the 1914-15 chalet still stands as trail-only lodging.

facts.design: Chalet built of local logs and stone
facts.status_note: The chalet stands and operates as lodging. No source describes a separate lookout structure there today.

access.note: Reached only by trail, and no vehicle access is provided. Belton Chalets, Inc. manages it as lodging.

visit.trail_note: Reached only by trail. No vehicle access is provided.

events.note: NPS says the chalet was built in 1914 and 1915 by the Great Northern Railway. Wikipedia's infobox gives 1913; its text gives 1914.
NPS report, as quoted by Montana Lookouts: two new lookouts installed in 1930, one at Granite Park Chalets.
The same report says the lookout was operated by the porter at the chalets, as a courtesy of the Glacier Park Hotel Co.
Added to the National Register of Historic Places on June 27, 1983.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NPS says the chalet was built in 1914 and 1915. Wikipedia's text says 1914 and its infobox says 1913. The story uses the NPS dates and notes the Wikipedia infobox.

notes_for_editor: The 1930 lookout comes from a Montana Lookouts index page that quotes a 1930 NPS report. The original report was not located. The WillhiteWeb page calls the chalet-as-lookout reading provisional. No source gives an operating span, a staffing end date or a removal date for the lookout. The brief's record Granite Park Chalets refers to the chalet, not a separate tower. The NPS page has a typo ('Chelt') and was not quoted for it.
